patients.summary: Administrative assistant on Medicaid with type 2 diabetes, hypertension and severe obesity who joins in 2021, has a Roux-en-Y bypass in 2022 complicated by an anastomotic leak, then in 2025-2026 is found to have Cushing syndrome with an L1 fracture, a gastrojejunal stricture, B12 deficiency anemia, erysipelas and septic cavernous sinus thrombosis. Endocrinology localization of the Cushing syndrome is the open thread at today.

documents.title: Prior primary care records summary
documents.author: front desk
documents.body:
Records received by fax from patient's previous primary care office ahead of her new patient visit next week. 41 pages. Includes visit notes 2017-2021, med list, labs, immunizations.

Highlights pulled for the PCP:
- Type 2 diabetes, on metformin 1000 mg BID. Last A1c in their records 8.9 (spring 2021).
- Hypertension on lisinopril 20 mg daily.
- Obesity, weight 116-120 kg over the last 3 years.
- Several sinus infections treated with antibiotics over the years.
- Pap 2019: NILM, HPV negative.
- Screening mammogram 2020: BI-RADS 1.
- NKDA.
- Tdap last 2010. No pneumococcal vaccine on file.

Scanned to chart under Outside Records.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

45F transferring care from another primary care office (records reviewed, in chart). Wants a doctor she can actually reach; her last office kept changing providers on her.

HPI: Type 2 DM dx about 8 years ago, on metformin 1000 BID, never on anything else. Says she takes it most days, GI upset when she started but settled. Doesn't check sugars, no meter at home. Last A1c in outside records 8.9. HTN on lisinopril 20, no side effects. Weight has been 115-120 kg for years. Has tried calorie counting, a commercial program twice, walking at lunch. Loses 5-8 kg then it comes back. Asking about weight loss surgery, her insurance covers it now and a coworker had it done.
Also gets sinus infections a couple of times a year, usually treated with antibiotics at urgent care. None now.

PMH: T2DM, HTN, obesity, recurrent sinusitis
PSH: none
Meds: metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily
Allergies: NKDA
FHx: mother T2DM. Father HTN. Maternal aunt with severe obesity.
SHx: Administrative assistant at a property management office. Lives alone in an apartment in town. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.

ROS: no chest pain, dyspnea, polyuria, vision change, numbness of the feet. Snoring per a past partner, no witnessed apneas known.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet. Ht 163 cm, wt 118 kg, BMI 44.4.
Well appearing, pleasant. HEENT normal, no sinus tenderness. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen obese, soft, nontender. Ext no edema. Feet: skin intact, monofilament intact bilaterally, DP pulses 2+.

A/P:
1. Type 2 diabetes, not at goal. A1c today. Discussed options including adding a second agent; she would rather pursue bariatric surgery first, which is reasonable given BMI over 40 with comorbidities. Continue metformin.
2. Hypertension, controlled on lisinopril 20. CMP, UACR.
3. Severe obesity, BMI 44. Referral to bariatric surgery program placed.
4. Recurrent sinusitis by history, quiet now.
5. HM: Tdap and PCV20 today. HCV and HIV screening once, ordered. Screening mammogram ordered. Pap up to date (2019 co-test negative). Colon screening at 45, will start FIT next year after we see where surgery lands. Flu and COVID booster at a nurse visit in October.

RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Michelle, your labs are back. A1c 8.8, which is about what your old office had, so diabetes is not well controlled yet. Kidney function, potassium, thyroid and blood count all normal. No protein in the urine. LDL cholesterol is a bit high. Hepatitis C and HIV screens negative. The bariatric program should call you in the next couple of weeks; let me know if you don't hear from them.

reports.text: Bilateral digital screening mammogram with tomosynthesis. Comparison: prior outside study 2020. Breast composition: scattered areas of fibroglandular density. No suspicious mass, architectural distortion or suspicious calcifications. Skin and nipples normal. Axillae unremarkable.

documents.title: Mammogram result letter
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Dear Ms. Tremblay, your screening mammogram on 9/14/2021 was normal (no sign of cancer). Please continue routine screening. A copy has been sent to your doctor.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Came in on her lunch hour. Flu vaccine L deltoid, Pfizer booster R deltoid (primary series at a pharmacy in spring, card seen). Tolerated well, waited 15 min, no reaction. VIS given.

documents.title: Bariatric Surgery Consultation
documents.author: bariatric surgery
documents.body:
Regional Bariatric Surgery Program
Date of consultation: 10/19/2021

Thank you for referring Ms. Tremblay, 45, for surgical weight loss evaluation.

She has had obesity since her twenties, with multiple supervised diet attempts. Comorbidities: type 2 diabetes (most recent A1c 8.8), hypertension. No GERD symptoms. Never smoker, no alcohol. Medications metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily. NKDA.

Exam: Ht 163 cm, Wt 117.6 kg, BMI 44.3. BP 132/84. Abdomen obese, soft, no hernias, no prior incisions.

Assessment: Class III obesity with diabetes. Good candidate for laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, which offers the best metabolic benefit for her diabetes. Risks reviewed at length, including leak, stricture, marginal ulcer, internal hernia, dumping and lifelong vitamin and mineral deficiencies requiring supplements and monitoring.

Plan: 6-month program: dietitian visits, psychology evaluation, support group, preoperative clearance from PCP closer to the date. We will send the clearance request.

Bariatric Surgery

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u DM, HTN. Saw the bariatric program in October, is in their 6 month prep program, had first dietitian visit, likes her. Down about a kilo. Taking metformin consistently now, set a phone alarm.

No hypoglycemia sx. No chest pain or SOB.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Heart RRR, lungs clear, no edema.

A/P
T2DM: A1c today. Continue metformin 1000 BID. Surgery likely to help more than any drug I'd add right now; revisit if A1c rises.
HTN: at goal on lisinopril 20.
Obesity: in bariatric prep program.
RTC 3-4 months or for pre-op clearance when the program asks.

documents.title: Diabetic Eye Examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body:
Optometry report to PCP. Exam 12/02/2021.
Dilated fundus exam both eyes. Best corrected acuity 20/20 OD, 20/25 OS. IOP 15/16. Lens clear. Optic nerves healthy, cup-to-disc 0.3 OU. Maculae flat. No hemorrhages, exudates or neovascularization.
Impression: No diabetic retinopathy OU. Mild myopia, glasses updated.
Recommend repeat dilated exam in 12 months.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Bariatric program called. Pt has a surgery date of 4/21 for laparoscopic gastric bypass, needs PCP pre-op evaluation with ECG and CBC/BMP within 30-60 days. Form faxed. Scheduled pt 3/8 at 8:20.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate 76. PR 158 ms, QRS 88 ms, QTc 421 ms. Normal axis. No ST or T wave abnormality. No prior for comparison.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
PRE-OP EVALUATION
Procedure: laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, 4/21/2022, bariatric program.

Completed the program steps (dietitian, psychology, support group). Down about 4 kg since joining here. Excited, a bit nervous.

Functional capacity: climbs 2 flights at work without stopping, walks 30 min most days. >4 METs. No chest pain, syncope, orthopnea, palpitations. No prior anesthesia, no family hx of anesthesia problems. No bleeding history.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20 daily. NKDA.

Exam: vitals in flowsheet, wt 114 kg. Airway: mouth opening normal, full neck ROM. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear. Abd obese, soft. No edema.

ECG: sinus, normal.

Assessment: 45F, low-risk surgery profile from a cardiac standpoint, no active cardiac conditions, good functional capacity. RCRI 0 (not on insulin). Acceptable risk to proceed.
Recs:
- Hold metformin the morning of surgery, hold lisinopril the morning of surgery.
- Labs today (CBC, BMP, A1c) will be faxed to program.
- Post-op supplement regimen per bariatric program.

Form completed and faxed.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass
documents.author: bariatric surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, bariatric surgery service
Admitted 04/21/2022, discharged 04/23/2022

Procedure 04/21/2022: Laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (antecolic, 150 cm Roux limb, small gastric pouch, stapled gastrojejunostomy). Estimated blood loss minimal. No intraoperative complications. Leak test negative at the end of the case.

Hospital course: Uneventful. Advanced to bariatric clear liquids POD 1, tolerated. Ambulating, pain controlled with oral medication by POD 2. Afebrile, heart rate 70s-80s at discharge. Glucose 120s-150s.

Discharge medications:
- Metformin 1000 mg twice daily (resume)
- Lisinopril 20 mg daily
- Cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily (new, lifelong)
- Calcium carbonate with vitamin D 600 mg/400 units twice daily (new, separate from multivitamin)
- Multivitamin 1 tablet daily, chewable for the first month (new)
Allergies: NKDA

Diet: bariatric full liquid stage for 2 weeks per handout.
Return precautions: fever, increasing abdominal pain, fast heart rate, shortness of breath, vomiting.
Follow-up in bariatric clinic in 2 weeks; PCP in 2-4 weeks.

reports.text: Single upright portable AP view. Lungs are clear without focal consolidation, effusion or pneumothorax. Heart size normal. No free intraperitoneal air beneath the hemidiaphragms. Postsurgical staple lines in the left upper quadrant.
reports.conclusion: No free air under the diaphragm. No acute cardiopulmonary process.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Anastomotic Leak
documents.author: general surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital, general surgery
Admitted 04/26/2022 via the emergency department. Discharged 05/06/2022.

Reason for admission: Five days after laparoscopic Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (04/21), two days of worsening abdominal pain, fever and shortness of breath.

Presentation: T 38.7 C, HR 110, RR 22, BP 135/85. Abdomen distended and diffusely tender to palpation; no rebound, no guarding. WBC 14.0, Hgb 12.5, platelets 250, creatinine 1.0, BUN 18, glucose 180. Upright chest film without free air.

Given tachycardia, fever and pain early after bypass, she was taken emergently to the OR the same night.

Procedure 04/26/2022: Diagnostic laparoscopy converted to exploratory laparotomy. Leak identified at the gastrojejunal anastomosis with localized contamination in the left upper quadrant. Primary repair with omental buttress, washout, two closed suction drains placed.

Hospital course: Broad-spectrum IV piperacillin-tazobactam. NPO with IV fluids, then clear liquids from POD 5 and advanced to bariatric full liquids. Metformin held while NPO and resumed on diet. Drains removed POD 8 and 9. Fevers resolved by day 3, white count normalized. Midline incision clean, staples out at bariatric clinic follow-up.

Diagnosis: Anastomotic leak (gastrojejunostomy) after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, repaired.

Discharge medications: unchanged from 04/23 (metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg daily, calcium carbonate/vitamin D 600 mg/400 units BID, multivitamin daily). Antibiotics completed in hospital.
Allergies: NKDA.
Follow-up: bariatric surgery clinic 1 week; PCP 1 week.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after gastric bypass and leak repair

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-discharge visit. Bypass 4/21, back 4/26 with a leak at the GJ anastomosis, ex-lap and repair, home 5/6. Discharge summary reviewed.

Feels weak and tired but much better. Pain mostly at the midline incision, using less of the pain medicine each day. Tolerating full liquids, protein shakes 3/day, sipping water all day. No fever, no vomiting. BMs every 2 days.

Taking metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, B12 1000 mcg, calcium/D BID, multivitamin. Sugars in the hospital 120s-150s.

Exam: afebrile, HR 84, BP ok. Looks tired. Midline incision healing, no erythema or drainage, drain sites dry and closed. Abdomen soft, appropriately tender near incision. Lungs clear.

A/P
1. S/p RYGB complicated by anastomotic leak, repaired. Recovering. Leak resolved per surgery. CBC/BMP today. Bariatric clinic Friday.
2. T2DM: continue metformin for now. If intake stays low and sugars drop, may need to lower; she'll call with any shakiness or sweats.
3. HTN: BP fine, continue lisinopril; may need less as weight falls.
4. Supplements as above, lifelong.
RTC 2-3 months.

documents.title: Bariatric Surgery Follow-up
documents.author: bariatric surgery
documents.body:
Bariatric surgery clinic, 3-month postoperative visit 07/21/2022.

Doing well after a difficult start (leak, repaired). Eating soft solids, small portions, protein goal met most days. No vomiting, no dysphagia, no dumping. Weight 98.6 kg, down from 114 kg preoperatively.

Incision healed. Taking cyanocobalamin, calcium with vitamin D and multivitamin as prescribed.

Plan: continue supplements lifelong. Labs at 6 and 12 months. Annual visits thereafter. Reminder to avoid NSAIDs.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
ANNUAL PHYSICAL

46F, 6 months out from RYGB (leak, repaired). Feels like a different person. Down about 25 kg from pre-op, 93 kg today. Eating 3 small meals + protein snacks. Walking 40 min at lunch. No vomiting, no dysphagia, occasional loose stool after sweets which she now avoids. Taking all supplements.
No sinus infections this year.

Meds: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, cyanocobalamin 1000 mcg, calcium/D 600/400 BID, MVI.
Allergies: NKDA

ROS otherwise negative. Periods regular.

Exam: BMI 35.2. Well appearing. HEENT nl. Thyroid nl. Heart RRR, lungs clear. Breasts deferred to mammogram. Abd: healed midline and port scars, soft, NT. Skin: no lesions of concern. Ext no edema. Feet: monofilament intact, pulses 2+.

A/P
- T2DM: A1c today; expect a big improvement. Continue metformin for now.
- HTN: 126/80 on lisinopril 20. Continue.
- S/p RYGB: supplements lifelong, bariatric clinic is checking micronutrients.
- HM: flu + bivalent COVID today. FIT kit given (age 46, average risk). Mammogram due next fall. Pap due 2024. PHQ-2 0.
RTC 6 months.

documents.title: Physical labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Michelle, great news: A1c is down to 6.9 from 8.8 last year. Kidney and liver tests normal, blood count normal, urine protein normal. LDL still in the high 120s. Keep up the walking. Remember to send back the FIT kit.

documents.title: RE: Physical labs
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thank you!! I cried a little. Will mail the kit this week.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: FIT negative. Pt notified by portal per PCP. Repeat in 1 year.
